feature: Build the Discipulado IEADPE Flutter web-first application with scoped ministry administration and attendance
global_constraints: Implement in a new Flutter project root; preserve the legacy Android folder and its data.
Flutter web is the release target; support keyboard, pointer, touch, browser history, direct links, refresh, and responsive layouts.
User-facing copy uses pt-BR; identifiers, code, specifications, and technical documentation use English.
Use Firebase Auth, Firestore, and authenticated callable functions with a new schema; never reuse legacy credentials or production data.
The backend enforces authorization and validation; hiding controls or filtering fetched data in Flutter is not authorization.
Use stable opaque IDs, ISO date-only strings for calendar dates, UTC server timestamps for events, and integer revisions for mutable records.
Online writes require server confirmation; no offline write queue, automatic retry of mutations, persistent sensitive browser cache, or false success messages.
Resolve compatible dependencies and commit lockfiles during implementation; no template or extension search is required.
Keep feature logic separate from widgets and vendor SDKs; use injected repositories and deterministic clocks in tests.
Do not deploy, push, import legacy data, or send messages automatically. Build and emulator verification are the release evidence for the implementation handoff.
All spec sections are normative. The plan paths refer to a separate new repository with Flutter at its root; copy spec.md and plan.json there before execution.

Each touches entry is an exact production/configuration/documentation path exclusively owned by that task. New test files are authored during implementation and omitted from touches to satisfy the installed brief-scaffold contract.

Tasks consume the exact models and ports in S05 and S11. Widgets never call Firebase directly. Implement and test modules before final entry-point composition; do not create temporary main.dart or functions/src/index.ts files in earlier tasks.

Each task runs under the gate of its own ecosystem, never a single branch-wide gate. Before dispatching a task, Script CEO appends the matching `gate` ledger entry: Flutter tasks use the `two-model-coder` operador with `flutter test`/`flutter analyze`; backend `functions/` tasks use the installed `two-model-coder-node` operador with the Node build/test commands and Node-format RED evidence. The auto-detected root `pubspec.yaml` -> flutter entry does not execute or classify the TypeScript backend and must not dispatch backend tasks. A backend task dispatched without the Node gate is an environment blocker under S13/S14, never a reason to weaken acceptance or fall back to production data or fake repositories. Use the pipeline command wrapper when executing through the two-model runner.
Use only synthetic fixtures. Release evidence must distinguish executed checks from environment-blocked checks. No acceptance item may be closed on the basis of fake repositories in the final app.

Design tokens are defined exactly once, in lib/ui/app_theme.dart owned by task 8: primary #002060, secondary #00A3E0, accent #E31B23, white is permitted as a neutral surface. Semantic tokens must meet WCAG AA contrast (text >= 4.5:1, control boundary/focus >= 3:1) in both light and dark modes; dark mode ships dark surfaces with the same color language and sufficient contrast, never inverted text. All simple visual polish (spacing scale, button corner radius and consistent shape system, control heights, small radii) is implemented inside task 8 as one unit, not scattered across feature tasks.

Task dispatch respects the declared dependency graph: Script CEO must not dispatch a task until every task in its `depends_on` is recorded `task_complete` in the ledger. A task dispatched before an exclusively-owned dependency is delivered (for example, task 7 consuming the `lib/ui` primitives owned exclusively by task 8) is an environment/scheduling blocker under S13/S14, never a TEST_DEFECT and never a reason to weaken acceptance, re-scope touches, or bypass the exclusive owner. Dispatch the unmet dependency first.

Working-tree hygiene and scope attribution: a task's gate, including its RED/GREEN evidence and the coder-gate scope check, evaluates only the artifacts that task itself authors. Uncommitted changes left in the tree by an earlier failed, escalated, or interrupted attempt of another task (for example the aborted task 7 attempt's `lib/data/` files, owned exclusively by task 7 and never committed) are foreign work, not a scope violation of the dispatched task. Before dispatching a task, Script CEO must restore the tree to the last recorded `task_complete` commit by discarding or stashing such foreign changes, and must commit the director's plan.json edits and pin the recorded `plan_sha` before scaffolding the next brief; an uncommitted director plan edit must never be attributed to a task's scope. A `scope_violation` whose only out-of-scope paths belong to another task's unfinished attempt is an environment/tree-hygiene blocker under S13/S14, never a task viability defect, and it must not weaken the dispatched task's acceptance, re-scope its touches, or blame the implementation. A task whose attempt ended in escalation, TEST_DEFECT, or a gate failure is not `task_complete`; it restarts from the clean post-dependency state, and a dependency (task 7 depends on task 8) is never bypassed by reusing leftover artifacts from that failed attempt.

tasks.title: Define the Flutter domain and shared contracts
tasks.summary: Establish root Flutter package configuration, dependencies, immutable domain types, validation, and injected ports from S05/S11. This is the sole owner of Dart package manifests and contracts consumed by subsequent modules; the executable entry point is composed in task 13.
acceptance: The new root resolves a mutually compatible locked Flutter/Dart dependency set for the libraries named in S11, UUID generation, flutter_test and integration_test; no Android source or legacy configuration is copied. Only dependencies actually used by the final planned app are declared.
All models, enum values, common metadata, scope ownership and ports in S05/S11 exist with immutable values and explicit JSON serialization; calendar dates do not shift through UTC conversion.

AuthRepository, BackendGateway, QueryRequest, RecordLocator, PageResult and AppFailure follow S11 signatures; resource identifiers cannot address users, internal role/uniqueness indexes, receipts or roster directly through generic query APIs.

Validation accepts Brazilian formatted or normalized phone input, rejects malformed structure, accepts empty optional fields, preserves Unicode display names, and produces matching normalized name keys for accented examples.

New unit tests under test/domain/ cover leap-year acceptance/rejection, impossible dates, future birth dates with a fixed Recife clock, an age below ten without artificial rejection, optional religious answers, contradictory baptism answers and unknown enum decoding.
Progress unit tests prove 3 present plus 1 absent plus 2 excused yields 75%, zero denominator has no percentage, and open/canceled sessions do not contribute.
Domain tests run without Firebase or widgets; flutter analyze succeeds on the package and no app main entry point is introduced in this task.

tasks.title: Establish backend authorization and transaction infrastructure
tasks.summary: Create the TypeScript backend foundation, scoped read rules, indexes, validation and idempotent command infrastructure. Supply emulator configuration and trusted access-profile provisioning so later handlers cannot rely on client-side permissions.
acceptance: Backend package scripts provide build, unit-test and emulator-test entry points with compatible locked dependencies; these are the commands the backend Node gate runs, not the Flutter gate. firebase.json declares local Auth, Firestore and Functions emulators and the eventual web SPA hosting rewrite without a production project binding.

An authorize-context helper reads the current user profile and congregation on every call, rejects missing/inactive profiles, and enforces supervisor versus congregationStaff scope; roles supplied in payloads grant no access.

Firestore rules deny all client writes and unspecified reads, expose only an authenticated minimal directory and active congregation names, allow own access-profile reads, and scope private congregational records according to S04. Supervision contacts and archived congregation reads are supervisor-protected.

Index definitions cover the shipped equality filters and sort orders in S09, including compound scope/role/name directory queries, archived/name students, class/status/name, session class/date/status and enrollment class/student/status/date. A query matrix test enumerates the supported combinations.

The command wrapper validates requestId and payload digest, authorizes even cached receipt retrieval, transactionally persists seven-day receipts with results, and returns the prior result only for an identical replay. Stable-ID creates reject existing unrelated records; stale revisions fail without writes.
Backend validation matches Dart examples for names, dates, nullable booleans, enum values, phone normalization and lengths. Unknown fields are rejected rather than copied into Admin SDK writes.

New emulator tests under functions/test/security/ prove anonymous reads/writes, cross-congregation private reads, forged paths, user-profile self-escalation and deactivated-account operations are denied; directory records omit birth date, address and all student fields.

Trusted provisioning accepts an existing Auth UID, access role, active flag and valid congregation binding; it is not exported as a callable. Synthetic seeds refuse to operate unless emulator environment variables are present and never load the legacy credential file.
Backend compilation and infrastructure tests pass under the backend Node gate without functions/src/index.ts; feature callables are registered only by task 13.

Verification for this task is dispatched under the backend Node gate (`two-model-coder-node`, Node test/analyze commands): the RED artifact is Node/Vitest machine-readable output at the task RED path, and the authoritative gate compiles and unit-tests functions/. This task is never dispatched under the auto-detected Flutter gate, whose flutter test/flutter analyze neither executes nor classifies the backend suite; if the Node gate cannot be configured, report an environment blocker under S13/S14 rather than weakening this acceptance.

tasks.title: Implement congregation and team transactions
tasks.summary: Implement congregation lifecycle and contact operations over the task 2 authorized transaction boundary. Preserve single-holder administrative functions and multiple teachers without using names as IDs or deleting displaced contacts.
acceptance: Exports define saveCongregation, setCongregationArchived, saveContact, replaceRoleHolder and setContactArchived using S11 payload/result conventions, with callable wrappers separate from injectable services.

Supervisors create uniquely normalized congregation names, rename without changing ID, and archive/restore; archive is blocked by active users, unarchived students/contacts or active classes. Staff cannot mutate congregations or supervision contacts.
Homonymous contacts coexist, renaming retains ID/createdAt, scope is immutable, and invalid role/scope combinations fail validation. Role codes and labels match all twelve S06 entries.

Administrative role claims use per-scope transactional slots; teacher permits multiple holders. Replacement checks both revisions, clears only the old assignment, preserves the old person, and commits all affected directory projections and receipt atomically.

Archiving removes active directory availability and releases role assignment atomically; restoring reintroduces an unassigned active contact. A teacher referenced by an active class cannot be archived or lose teacher eligibility.
Directory rendering uses the authoritative congregation name by ID after rename and never exposes birth date. Private fields remain solely in the scoped full record.

New tests under functions/test/contacts/ and functions/test/congregations/ prove concurrent same-role attempts yield exactly one holder, failed replacement leaves all documents unchanged, distinct scopes may use the same role, duplicate request replay is safe, and local staff cannot edit another scope.

tasks.title: Implement student persistence and class-filtered reads
tasks.summary: Provide scoped student create/edit/archive/restore and the callable query needed for active-class filtering. Enforce private-record ownership and preserve identity and history independently of the student's name.
acceptance: Exports define saveStudent, setStudentArchived and listClassStudents using S11 authorization, validation, revision and receipt contracts.

Name is the only required personal field; optional education, marital status, address, phone, birth date and nullable religious answers follow S05 limits. Neither same name nor missing optional information blocks a distinct student.

Edit preserves ID and creation metadata and cannot change congregation; stale revision cannot overwrite another edit. Archive is blocked by active enrollment and retains history; restore uses the existing ID.

listClassStudents validates class scope, resolves active enrollment membership and applies prefix ordering/search before page limits; no page is filtered after an unrelated student page was fetched. Cursors bind scope, filter and ordering.
Query results never include another congregation's students, and unknown/out-of-scope IDs produce a safe not-found/forbidden failure without personal data.

New tests under functions/test/students/ cover homonyms, rename identity, active-enrollment archive denial, rollback, idempotent creation, forged congregation IDs, and class-filter pagination where matching students lie beyond the first unfiltered page.

The student flow maintains `congregations/{id}/internal/references.unarchivedStudents` inside the same transaction that creates, archives or restores a student (increment on unarchived create/restore, decrement on archive), so the congregation archive guard is driven by real student operations; its tests exercise that dependency through the real create/archive operation instead of seeding the internal reference document directly.

tasks.title: Implement classes and enrollment lifecycle
tasks.summary: Implement class and enrollment invariants over the authorized backend transaction boundary. Preserve student history, enforce eligible teachers and cohort capacity, and provide stable records for attendance operations in task 6.
acceptance: Exports define saveClass, setClassStatus, enrollStudent and closeEnrollment with the exact operation names and command contracts in S11.

Class teacher must be a local active teacher contact. Dates, active/completed/archived transitions, enrollment/session prerequisites and read-only completed-class behavior follow S08 and are backend-enforced.

Enrollment accepts only unarchived same-congregation students and active classes. Per-student active enrollment uniqueness and the cap of 100 total enrollment records including closed records are transactionally enforced; closing an enrollment does not free historical capacity.

Close records completed or withdrawn plus an explicit valid end date without deleting history. Once present in a frozen roster, startDate cannot change; closing remains allowed when endDate is at least the latest noncanceled frozen session date containing the enrollment. Student, class and teacher IDs from other congregations are denied.

Class completion is blocked by active enrollments or open sessions. Dates cannot change after any enrollment/session exists; completed classes are immutable except archival. Active empty classes alone may be archived directly.

New tests under functions/test/enrollments/ and functions/test/classes/ prove anonymous/cross-scope denial, concurrent enrollment exclusivity, capacity at 100 versus 101 including closed records, teacher eligibility, stale revision, request replay and class lifecycle constraints using synthetic session/roster fixtures.

The class flow maintains `congregations/{id}/internal/references.activeClasses` inside the same transaction that creates, completes, archives or reactivates a class, and its tests prove the congregation archive guard through the real class lifecycle rather than a directly seeded reference document.

tasks.title: Implement session rosters and atomic attendance
tasks.summary: Build session and attendance transactions on the class/enrollment model. Freeze historical membership, protect concurrent submissions and return explicit per-enrollment progress without inferring graduation.
acceptance: Exports define createSession, saveAttendance, cancelSession, getSessionAttendance and getEnrollmentProgress with the exact operation names in S11.

Session uniqueness is per class/date for noncanceled sessions. First saved attendance freezes eligible enrollment intervals and historical names from authoritative records. Late enrollment cannot silently alter the roster.

Attendance accepts exactly the complete roster map with present/absent/excused/unmarked, checks expected session revision and atomically commits roster, marks, session revision and receipt. Injected failure leaves all documents unchanged.

Finalization rejects empty/incomplete rosters and future dates; save-and-finalize is atomic. Authorized correction retains finalized status and frozen membership; cancellation preserves history and excludes it from progress. Completed classes reject attendance mutations.

Progress returns counts and nullable percentage per enrollment; only finalized noncanceled sessions contribute, excused is excluded, 3 present plus 1 absent yields 75%, and zero denominator remains absent rather than 0%.

New tests under functions/test/attendance/ prove frozen-roster behavior, historical names, duplicate session/date, stale saves, idempotent retry, partial-write rollback, correction, cancellation and capacity-bounded transaction behavior. Every handler denies anonymous and cross-congregation access.

tasks.title: Connect individual sessions and scoped Flutter data access
tasks.summary: Implement Firebase adapters and authentication controllers/pages over the domain ports. Centralize safe errors, query/cursor construction, and in-memory session cleanup before any feature UI depends on remote data.
acceptance: AuthRepository implements individual sign-in, generic password-reset response and sign-out with session-scoped persistence; public registration and congregation/password matching are absent.

watchSession resolves both Firebase identity and an active access profile. Missing/inactive profiles show Acesso não autorizado; profile revocation/scope change clears controllers and listeners before another protected frame renders.

Firebase configuration is supplied explicitly per environment, emulator mode is clearly labeled, persistent Firestore browser caching is disabled, and absent configuration reports a setup error without fallback to legacy credentials.

BackendGateway implements validated resource reads and stable cursor queries, routes complex query operations to their S11 callable names, translates SDK errors to AppFailure, and rejects internal collection/resource access.

Mutation payloads retain UUID and requestId for explicit retry, successful UI state requires a server response, timeout preserves draft and retry identity, and no mutation retries itself automatically.

Authentication pages use shared accessible controls, preserve safe internal return destinations for final router composition, prevent external redirect targets, and never log passwords or account/profile payloads.

New tests under test/data/ and test/features/auth/ cover profile loading, inactive access, sign-out cleanup, cross-scope cursor reuse, stale query responses, network errors, retained retry IDs and pt-BR field feedback. Auth emulator integration proves a valid password alone does not bypass profile authorization.
Auth pages and controls consume app_theme.dart tokens and lib/ui primitives exclusively; no hardcoded colors, corner radii, spacing or duplicated control styling, in light or dark mode.

tasks.title: Create responsive and accessible shared presentation
tasks.summary: Build the reusable visual primitives, theme tokens, asynchronous states and navigation shell structure for a browser-oriented administration app. Define the entire visual language here in one unit: brand colors, spacing, shape/radius system, control heights, dark mode. Apply the measurable apple-design interaction criteria in S10 without adding gesture or animation frameworks; feature tasks consume these primitives and never re-themed controls.
acceptance: Layout follows S10 breakpoints: persistent navigation at >=1024, compact at 600–1023, drawer/cards below 600. Reusable lists and forms reflow at 360/768/1440 and 200% text without clipped primary actions or page-wide horizontal scroll.

Theme tokens are defined once in app_theme.dart: primary #002060, secondary #00A3E0, accent #E31B23, with white as a permitted neutral surface. Light and dark themes share this color language; every semantic token combination used for text meets >= 4.5:1 and every control boundary/focus indication meets >= 3:1 in both modes, verified by measured token tests.

The theme applies platform typography, body size >=16, a consistent 4/8 spacing scale, >=44x44 touch targets, a unified control shape system (button corner radius applied consistently across all buttons) and control heights — all implemented here as one unit, with no scattered restyling in feature tasks.

Buttons provide immediate press/focus feedback but invoke actions only on activation. Keyboard navigation, dialog focus trap, Escape cancellation and trigger focus restoration work with semantic labels and outcome announcements.

Reduced motion eliminates positional animation and overshoot; default reversible transitions stay interruptible and preserve form state. Any translucent chrome has an opaque reduced-transparency/high-contrast fallback.

AsyncContent distinguishes initial loading, empty dataset, empty search, error/retry, forbidden and not-found. Forms associate validation errors with fields and focus the first invalid input after submit.
DirtyFormGuard exposes integration hooks for in-app routing, browser history and supported unload confirmation, while never persisting a sensitive draft locally.

New widget tests under test/ui/ verify reflow/text scaling, keyboard-only dialog operations, reduced-motion behavior, error focus, long accented names, disabled/submitting control semantics, and contrast compliance for text and focus tokens in light and dark modes.

tasks.title: Build team directory and congregation workflows
tasks.summary: Deliver searchable team contacts, scoped editors, administrative-role replacement and supervisor congregation management. Use the minimal directory projection outside a caller's private scope and explicit user actions for external contact.
acceptance: Equipe supports name-prefix search, role/scope filters, explicit pagination and refresh with stable ordering; filters are exposed as route state for task 13 and changing filters resets pagination.

Cross-scope contact detail requests only the directory projection; authorized local/supervisor editors can create, rename, archive and restore by stable ID using the six S06 operations. Birth dates never appear in the directory UI.

All role labels match S06; occupied administrative roles show the existing holder and explicit replacement confirmation. Cancel sends no mutation; conflict preserves inputs and offers reload; success keeps the old contact unassigned rather than deleting it.

Supervisors manage congregation lifecycle with backend dependency errors rendered as actionable explanations. Staff see no write controls for congregations or another scope, while backend denial still maps to a safe error.
WhatsApp links contain only normalized phone digits, are activated explicitly, never send/prefill sensitive data, and offer accessible copy-phone fallback. Missing phone has a labeled disabled state.

New tests under test/features/team/ and test/features/congregations/ cover homonym rendering, identity-preserving rename, loaded role preselection, replacement cancel/conflict, projection-only access, blocked archive, URL encoding and keyboard focus.
Team and congregation screens consume app_theme.dart tokens and lib/ui primitives exclusively; no hardcoded colors, corner radii, spacing or duplicated control styling, in light or dark mode.

tasks.title: Build student records and enrollment history
tasks.summary: Deliver scoped student lists, grouped forms, private detail and immutable enrollment history. Keep optional personal/religious data optional and connect enrollment progress to authoritative backend results.
acceptance: Alunos exposes scope, name-prefix search, archived and active-class filters, pagination, refresh and URL-state hooks. Staff scope is fixed and supervisor creation requires one selected congregation.

Create/edit require only name; personal/contact/discipleship groups preserve null for unanswered religious fields and follow S05 validation with pt-BR copy. Homonym information never replaces an existing record.
Student detail includes enrollment history and the S08 counts/percentage; zero denominator displays Sem aulas contabilizadas and there is no automatic graduation/baptism inference.
Archive/restore uses confirmation and existing ID; active-enrollment denial explains that enrollment must close first. Historical attendance and person identity remain unchanged.

Forms keep values on backend validation, conflict or unavailable errors, show success only after acknowledgment, warn before dirty navigation, and do not persist drafts or expose private fields in list rows/URLs.

New tests under test/features/students/ cover optional fields, leap-day input, same-name records, stale revision, dirty cancellation, class-filter pagination, scoped not-found, archive denial, progress rendering and keyboard submit.
Student screens consume app_theme.dart tokens and lib/ui primitives exclusively; no hardcoded colors, corner radii, spacing or duplicated control styling, in light or dark mode.

tasks.title: Build classes and explicit attendance editing
tasks.summary: Deliver class lifecycle, enrollment management, session creation and a four-state attendance editor. Preserve unsaved choices on conflicts and make the difference between saving and finalizing visible.
acceptance: Turmas provides scoped filters, paging, create and detail with teacher, dates, roster and session list. Only eligible teachers/students are selectable and backend failures retain the user's inputs.

Enrollment can start and close as completed/withdrawn with explicit dates; active-enrollment conflicts show the existing class, and capacity/date/frozen-roster limits have actionable messages. There is no cross-congregation transfer flow.
Session creation preserves date/topic, displays status, prevents duplicate submissions, and links to a deep-linkable attendance page using class and session IDs.

Every row exposes Presente, Ausente, Justificado and Não marcado with text/semantics as well as color. Initial load does not convert unmarked to absent. Marcar todos presentes is explicit and remains unsaved until Salvar chamada.

Save submits a complete roster map with expected session revision; timeout retains request identity and choices, conflict offers reload with a visible comparison copy, and no partial or stale response is announced as success.

Finalization explains incomplete/future-date failures, correction preserves frozen membership, cancellation requires confirmation and completed-class controls are read-only. Progress refreshes after successful changes.

New tests under test/features/classes/ and test/features/attendance/ cover keyboard-only marking, all four statuses, complete-map submission, finalization error, capacity boundary, stale save, cancellation, frozen historical names and narrow/text-scaled layout.
Class, session and attendance screens consume app_theme.dart tokens and lib/ui primitives exclusively; no hardcoded colors, corner radii, spacing or duplicated control styling, in light or dark mode.

tasks.title: Deliver scoped overview counts and navigation
tasks.summary: Provide authoritative dashboard counts and corresponding filtered navigation. Keep the overview limited to operational information grounded in the legacy discipleship concepts.
acceptance: getOverview returns counts of unarchived students, active classes and open sessions through today's Recife date, using authorized server queries rather than downloading all records to the browser.
Staff always receive their own congregation; supervision may select one or Todas. Caller-provided scope cannot expand staff access and inactive profiles are rejected.
Visão geral renders counts with clear labels and links carrying the same scope/filter to students, classes and open sessions; no zero count is fabricated when the endpoint fails.
Page entry, Atualizar and relevant successful mutations invalidate counts. Stale results from a previous congregation cannot appear after a scope switch.

New tests under functions/test/overview/ and test/features/overview/ verify two-congregation aggregation, canceled/future-session exclusion, archived-student exclusion, authorization, error/retry state and keyboard navigation links.

listPendingSessions provides the paginated overview section selected by pendentes=true, ordered by date/ID and scoped to the caller; each row links to the exact class/session with congregation ID. Tests cover authorized all-congregation paging and reject cursor reuse across scopes.
The overview page consumes app_theme.dart tokens and lib/ui primitives exclusively; no hardcoded colors, corner radii, spacing or duplicated control styling, in light or dark mode.

tasks.title: Compose the application and verify the browser release
tasks.summary: Wire the completed modules into one executable Flutter web application and export the backend callables. Add reproducible local/CI verification and the runbook, proving the complete emulator-backed flow without deployment or legacy access.
acceptance: Application entry points inject real AuthRepository, BackendGateway and feature repositories; emulator configuration remains explicit. Backend index exports every S11 callable exactly once and no unguarded provisioning endpoint.

All S10 routes work with deep links, hard refresh, browser back/forward and URL filter state. Session loading preserves internal destination; dirty forms get supported navigation protection; invalid IDs/paths show safe not-found/forbidden screens.

Signed-out users cannot display loaded private content, another congregation cannot reuse a forged scope/deep link, and profile deactivation/scope change disposes the old data. All accessible navigation labels and scope selectors match the specification.

New browser integration tests under integration_test/ exercise sign-in, contact homonym/rename/role replacement, student/class creation, enrollment, attendance save/finalization/progress, reload/history, sign-out and denied second-congregation access against real local emulators.

The verification entry points fail on Flutter analysis/tests/build, backend compilation/unit/emulator tests, or critical browser-flow failure; CI invokes the same entry points. Backend authorization checks cannot be bypassed by a green Flutter test suite.

Record executed commands, exit codes, actual browser/runtime versions and responsive/accessibility findings in docs/verification.md. Chromium end-to-end plus Firefox/WebKit smoke, 360/768/1440 layouts, 200% text, reduced motion and keyboard/screen-reader checks meet S13. Any environment-blocked check remains explicitly incomplete.

README documents dependency setup, locked runtimes, explicit emulator startup, synthetic fixtures, first-supervisor provisioning, dev login/reset, web build and SPA rewrite. It explains archive/history, class capacity and progress semantics without claiming production deployment or legal compliance.

The release build contains no Admin SDK credentials, legacy password arrays, sensitive fixture records or production fallbacks; runtime logs do not disclose people, phones or religious status. No placeholder screens or production fake repositories remain.
No push, deployment, message send, legacy import or Android packaging occurs; completed work is a locally runnable and verified Flutter web implementation ready for a separate release decision.

The composed shell, router, and not-found page consume app_theme.dart tokens and lib/ui primitives exclusively; no hardcoded colors, corner radii, spacing or duplicated control styling, in light or dark mode.

tasks.title: Correct the task 2 rules scoping and emulator-security findings
tasks.summary: Remediate the task 2 SEND_BACK findings within the existing backend foundation: replace the recursive nested wildcard in firestore.rules with explicit gated subcollection matches so archived congregations and internal uniqueness/roster records stay protected, make the emulator security entry point fail fast and non-skippable, bind the command digest to the requested scope, reject malformed stored profiles, and assert index scope/order.
acceptance: firestore.rules contains no recursive `{document=**}` wildcard under `/congregations/{congregationId}`. Each deliberately client-readable nested path (contacts, students, classes, enrollments, sessions, and any other path intentionally exposed by S04) is matched explicitly and gated by the congregation read predicate. Internal collections (role holder slots, roster, uniqueness/reservation records, receipts) are not enumerated and remain denied to direct client reads.

Because the explicit matches no longer match the parent `/congregations/{id}` document, only the active-congregation rule and the supervisor rule govern its read: congregationStaff is denied reading their own inactive/archived congregation while a supervisor is allowed. Rules stay deny-by-default for all writes and unspecified reads.

New emulator tests under functions/test/security/ prove a congregationStaff caller is denied reading their own inactive/archived congregation, a supervisor is allowed, and a direct client read of an internal uniqueness/roster document is denied; the existing anonymous and cross-scope denial matrix still passes.

The backend emulator-test entry point fails fast when required emulator environment variables (including FIRESTORE_EMULATOR_HOST) are absent: `npm run test:emulator` exits non-zero instead of silently skipping. A newly authored emulator test asserts real execution (via a sentinel the rules run must produce), so a run that skips the security suite can never report green; tests committed by earlier tasks are not modified.

The command wrapper payload digest binds operation, payload and requestedCongregationId, so replaying a requestId with a different requested scope is not served the prior scope's cached result; a unit test covers the scope-mismatch replay.

The altered-payload replay failure is either aligned with the S11 validation semantics or documented as a deliberate deviation with its chosen error code asserted, leaving no unrecorded mismatch between S11 wording and the implemented error.

Stored access profiles with malformed fields (non-integer/NaN revision, missing or invalid updatedAt, or other absent required fields) are rejected explicitly by authorize-context rather than coerced to NaN or a fabricated empty timestamp; a unit test covers the malformed profile.

Newly authored tests assert queryScope and order in addition to field-path sequences, and assert the exact expected S09 index definitions rather than a `length >= 8` count, hardening the S09 index guarantee.

Verification for this task is dispatched under the backend Node gate (`two-model-coder-node`, Node build/test commands). Backend compilation and tests pass and the Node gate is not weakened; if the gate cannot run, report an environment blocker under S13/S14.

All verification added by this task lives in newly authored test files. Tests committed by earlier tasks are never modified: a modified committed test is pipeline tampering, so every additional assertion is proven from a new file.

tasks.title: Restore the committed emulator denial matrix and harden the gate assertions
tasks.summary: Remediate the task 14 SEND_BACK findings: stop excluding the committed task-2 anonymous/cross-scope denial matrix from the emulator entry while keeping it excluded from non-emulator runs, and replace the task-14 gate test's raw-substring and working-tree-versus-index assertions with behavioral checks that fail on the bypass and compare the committed suite against its task-2 revision.
acceptance: functions/vitest.config.ts no longer lists test/security/rules.security.test.ts in the emulator-run `exclude`; `npm run test:emulator` loads and executes both the committed task-2 test/security/rules.security.test.ts anonymous/cross-scope denial matrix and the task-14 hardening suite. The non-emulator branches keep excluding test/security/**, so no entry point is widened to run security tests without emulators, and the committed matrix is no longer excluded from every entry point.

The emulator gate test's wiring assertion is behavioral, not raw substring presence: it proves the emulator run configuration includes both security suites and does not exclude test/security/rules.security.test.ts, and it fails against the previously buggy configuration that excluded the committed matrix instead of passing on the exclusion text. The FIRESTORE_EMULATOR_HOST fail-fast assertion remains.

The byte-identity guard compares test/security/rules.security.test.ts against an explicit base/task-2 revision (a git object or a pinned content hash), never the working tree against the index; it fails when the committed task-2 suite diverges from that revision, independent of commit state.

Only the task-14-authored gate test is edited. functions/test/security/rules.security.test.ts and every test committed by task 2 stay byte-identical to their committed revision, and no rule, guard or production check added by task 14 is weakened.

When the emulator environment is available, the executed run reports both security suites including the committed anonymous and cross-scope denial cases, so a run that still omits the matrix cannot be recorded as green; an environment-blocked execution is stated as incomplete, never as passed.

Verification is dispatched under the backend Node gate (`two-model-coder-node`, Node build/test commands); functions/ compiles and the non-emulator suite passes with the corrected gate assertions. If the Node gate or emulator environment cannot run, report an environment blocker under S13/S14 rather than weakening this acceptance.

tasks.title: Bind the validated name prefix to the Firestore query and de-race the emulator auth test
tasks.summary: Remediate the task 7 SEND_BACK Important findings: QueryCodec.plan validates and fingerprints QueryRequest.namePrefix but QueryPlan carries no prefix, so FirebaseDataTransport.runQuery silently returns unfiltered pages instead of S09 prefix matches; and the acceptance-mandated emulator denial test waits with pumpAndSettle, whose duration argument is an inter-frame budget, not a network wait, so the assertion can race the profile round-trip. Carry the normalized prefix through QueryPlan into the transport as a real range constraint preserved across cursors, and await the emulator denial result deterministically under a bounded timeout.
acceptance: QueryPlan carries the validated name prefix: QueryCodec.plan exposes a nullable namePrefix populated from QueryRequest.namePrefix whenever the prefix is allowed for the resource, normalized consistently with the stored normalized-name order key rather than re-fingerprinted from the raw input. A prefix is no longer validated and folded into filterFingerprint while being discarded from the plan; when the field is present, QueryPlan is the single source of the prefix for both cursor identity and query construction.

FirebaseDataTransport.runQuery applies the prefix to the Firestore query before paging: when plan.namePrefix is non-null it adds a range constraint on the plan's normalized-name order field (>= prefix and < prefix + '\uf8ff') combined with the existing equality filters, and only then applies startAfter/cursor paging. A prefix read over the resources that permit it (directory, students, classes) returns only normalized-name matches; it never returns the first N records ordered by normalizedName as if unfiltered, and the cursor fingerprint can no longer claim a prefix that the query does not bind.

Paging preserves the prefix: a continuation page fetched from a cursor spans the same range constraint, so every page of a prefixed query remains prefix-bounded and a cursor minted under a prefix is not accepted for a differently-scoped query (and vice versa). New tests under test/data/ assert that the transport receives the prefix condition and that a page-after page still carries it; no test proves prefix behavior only through the fingerprint, and the existing cross-scope cursor and stale-response assertions are preserved.

The emulator integration test no longer uses pumpAndSettle with a duration as a stand-in for a network wait. It awaits the profile-authorization outcome explicitly through a bounded future (a completer completed by the session error, awaited with a timeout such as 10 seconds) and asserts the expected AppFailure code only after that future resolves, so a slow or absent emulator response fails the test instead of racing it. The valid-password-alone denial claim and the happy-path assertion remain and none is weakened.

The correction stays inside the auth/data unit: the public AuthRepository and BackendGateway port contracts in S11 are unchanged (only the internal QueryPlan gains the prefix field), no feature UI is restyled, and no guard, validation or atomicity behavior added by task 7 is weakened. Tests committed by other completed tasks are never modified; the strengthened or new prefix-transport, cursor-paging and emulator-wait assertions live in newly authored test files or in the task-7-owned test files this correction is allowed to extend.

Verification is dispatched under the Flutter gate (`flutter test`/`flutter analyze`) with RED evidence from the added prefix-transport and cursor-paging tests failing against the pre-fix QueryPlan. The emulator integration test is executed when the local emulator environment is available; if it cannot run, that check is recorded as incomplete under S13/S14, never as passed, and the gate is not weakened.

tasks.summary: Remediate the task 9 SEND_BACK findings within the team/congregation feature: scope the administrative-holder lookup to the congregation through the directory query and the client query codec, resolve rendered congregation names from the authorized congregation catalog instead of the directory projection field that is never written, make both reload affordances refresh authoritative holder/revision data instead of only clearing the message, and give supervisors a real scoped read for supervision contacts so rename, archive and restore stop being silent no-ops.

Rendered congregation names are resolved from the authorized congregation catalog by congregationId, never from DirectoryEntry.congregationName: the TeamPage congregation column and the ContactPage detail line read the name through CongregationRepository (a catalog lookup or equivalent authorized read), fall back to a neutral placeholder instead of the raw congregation UUID when no name is available, and reflect a renamed congregation after a catalog refresh. The replacement and save reloads refresh authoritative data instead of only clearing the error: ContactForm passes an onReload to RoleReplacementDialog that re-runs findAdministrativeHolder for the selected role and re-reads the current holder record, updating both previousExpectedRevision and targetExpectedRevision while preserving the selected role and typed inputs, so a resubmit after a conflict can succeed; a save conflict on ContactForm likewise re-fetches the contact record to refresh expectedRevision rather than only clearing _failure. Supervisors get a real scoped read for supervision contacts: getContact no longer returns null for supervision scope; it resolves the full record and revision through the S11 BackendGateway.get port using a RecordLocator for the contact with no congregationId, which QueryCodec maps to the supervisor-protected supervisionContacts/{id} document path (never an internal collection and never a guessed congregation), so ContactPage loads the revision and Editar, Arquivar and Restaurar perform real mutations. tasks.title: Correct the task 12 handler-test, route-state and active-filter findings
tasks.summary: Remediate the task 12 SEND_BACK findings within the overview feature: make the callable handler tests exercise the real auth boundary (unauthenticated rejection and authenticated-UID override) instead of tautological type checks, give the controller an explicit `pendentes`/scope route-state surface with query-parameter round-tripping so task 13 can wire deep links and back/forward without editing task 12 files, carry the active class filter on the `Turmas ativas` link, and close the parked minors (pt-BR date rendering, cursor-stack ordering on failure, and a throughDate-bound cursor identity).
acceptance: The callable wrapper auth boundary is proven, not asserted by type: newly authored tests under functions/test/overview/ invoke the built callable path for `getOverviewCallable` and `listPendingSessionsCallable` (including the `requireUid` guard) with a request lacking `request.auth.uid` and assert an `AppError` with code `unauthenticated` and no service/read invocation; a second case sets `data.uid` to a different user while `request.auth.uid` is the real caller and asserts the service receives the authenticated UID (for example through a spy reader/datastore), never the payload value. If the current wrapper trusts a caller-supplied `uid`, functions/src/overview/handlers.ts is corrected so the authenticated identity overrides the payload. The prior `typeof x === 'function'`/not-same-object cases no longer stand as the coverage for acceptance 2/5; the new assertions fail against a wrapper that ignores auth or trusts `data.uid`.

The overview exposes an explicit route-state surface instead of a private local flip: lib/features/overview/overview_controller.dart makes an `OverviewQuery` value or an equivalent `setPendingVisible(bool)`/`initialPendingVisible` pair the single source of truth for `pendingVisible`, and provides `toQueryParameters`/`fromQueryParameters` covering the `congregacao` and `pendentes` keys, so task 13 (owner of lib/app/router.dart) can initialize the controller from the route and write back URL state without editing this task's files. `togglePending()` updates that same state (and the emitted query parameters), the existing scope selection is preserved, and a newly authored test proves `pendentes=true` round-trips to `pendingVisible == true` and back and that the exposed state — not a hidden boolean — drives the pending section.

The active-classes link carries the active filter: the `Turmas ativas` affordance passes `ClassStatus.active` (or an equally explicit navigation-contract value consumed by task 13) in addition to `congregationId`, so the target `/turmas` route shows the active class set the count represents rather than every class under the default `status == null`. A newly authored page test asserts that activating the classes count forwards both the scope and the active status filter, and the students and open-sessions links keep carrying their existing scope/filter; no zero count is fabricated on endpoint failure.

The parked minors from the task 12 review are closed inside the same files: the pending session row renders its date through the shared pt-BR `formatBrazilianDate` helper instead of raw `toIso8601String()`; lib/features/overview/overview_controller.dart updates its cursor stack only after the forward pending load resolves successfully, so a failed page fetch leaves no phantom previous-page entry; and functions/src/overview/service.ts includes the derived `throughDate` in cursor identity, so a cursor minted before the Recife date rollover is rejected the next day instead of paging page 2 against a new 'through today' window. Newly authored or strengthened tests cover each minor and fail against the pre-fix behavior.

Invalidation is testable and its remaining composition is recorded rather than silently claimed: page entry and the `Atualizar` affordance invoke the controller's invalidate entry point (proven by a test that observes the refresh/invalidity), and the controller exposes a stable public invalidation surface usable by composition. The outstanding call site — invoking invalidation from the relevant successful mutation flows — belongs to task 13 (lib/app/ composition), so this corrective records it as an explicit cross-task obligation for task 13 instead of reporting task 12 acceptance 4 as fully verified for mutation-driven invalidation.

Verification is split by ecosystem and neither gate is weakened: the functions/src/overview handler/cursor changes and the new functions/test/overview/ tests are dispatched under the backend Node gate (`two-model-coder-node`, Node build/test commands) with Node-format RED evidence, and the Dart controller/page changes and their tests are dispatched under the Flutter gate (`flutter test`/`flutter analyze`) with Flutter RED evidence. A green Flutter suite never stands in for the backend suite (or vice versa); if either required gate cannot run, report an environment blocker under S13/S14 rather than weakening the acceptance.

The correction stays inside the listed task-12 files: no S11 port contract, backend guard, validation or atomicity behavior is weakened, no existing acceptance behavior is deleted, and no test committed by another completed task is modified. New or strengthened tests live in newly authored test files or in the task-12-owned test files this correction may extend; no existing assertion is deleted or relaxed.

tasks.title: Run the task 26 backend half under the Node gate and record its evidence
tasks.summary: Remediate the task 26 SEND_BACK Critical finding: the corrected backend half was never executed under the backend Node gate, so the new functions/test/overview auth-boundary and throughDate-cursor assertions and the handlers/service changes are unverified green. Run the TypeScript build and the Node vitest/npm test commands for functions/test/overview/ under `two-model-coder-node`; capture Node-format RED evidence that the new assertions are non-vacuous against the pre-fix behavior and Node-format GREEN evidence from the current tree; and record an explicit S13/S14 environment blocker instead of substituting the Flutter suite if the Node toolchain cannot run.
acceptance: The backend half of task 26 is executed under the backend Node gate, not the Flutter gate: functions/test/overview/handlers.test.ts and functions/test/overview/pending_sessions.test.ts, together with the task-26 changes in functions/src/overview/handlers.ts and functions/src/overview/service.ts, are run through the `two-model-coder-node` operador using the functions build/compile and the Node vitest/`npm test` commands. The outcome is recorded as Node-format machine-readable artifacts at this task's Node RED and GREEN paths. Flutter artifacts (the scoped Flutter runner and the Flutter coder-gate, flutter test/flutter analyze) are not accepted as evidence for this backend half, and no Flutter-only artifact may be presented as proof that the functions tests or the handler/cursor changes pass.

Node RED evidence is produced in Node/Vitest format and demonstrates the task-26 assertions are non-vacuous: the auth-boundary cases in functions/test/overview/handlers.test.ts fail against the pre-fix wrapper (a request lacking request.auth.uid is not rejected with an `unauthenticated` AppError, and/or a caller-supplied data.uid overrides the authenticated identity), and the throughDate case in functions/test/overview/pending_sessions.test.ts fails against a cursor whose identity omits the derived throughDate. Because the fix is already committed, the pre-fix behavior may be reproduced by running the committed new tests against a minimally reverted copy of the handler/service in a disposable, uncommitted scratch checkout (auth-ignoring wrapper, uid-trusting payload, or cursor identity without throughDate) or by capturing an equivalent recorded pre-fix run. The committed task-26 tests are never modified, deleted or weakened to manufacture RED.

Node GREEN evidence from the current committed tree shows the full functions/test/overview/ suite and the TypeScript functions build/compile passing under the same Node gate, with the executed command and exit code recorded. A claimed or unexecuted Node result is not accepted and the task cannot be marked complete on the strength of the Flutter suite alone.

If the backend Node gate or its toolchain cannot be configured or run, the outcome is recorded as an explicit S13/S14 environment blocker naming the attempted command and the observed failure, and is reported as incomplete and environment-blocked. The Flutter suite is never substituted for the backend suite, and no acceptance is weakened to accommodate an unrunnable gate. This environment-blocker branch is valid only after the `two-model-coder-node` gate has been installed as the active gate (a `manual: node` ledger entry) and its Node commands were genuinely attempted; it is never a valid outcome of a dispatch that ran under the auto-detected Flutter gate.

This corrective is verification-only and stays inside the task-26 scope: it performs no production-code change and does not weaken any existing acceptance or assertion. The task-26 files, the task-12 files, and every test committed by earlier tasks remain byte-identical. If the Node run surfaces a genuine finding-scoped backend defect, it is reported as evidence for a further corrective rather than silently editing out-of-scope files; any test added here lives in a newly authored file.

Dispatch precondition (empty `touches`): because this verification-only task owns no files, the branch-wide toolchain detection (root pubspec.yaml, resolved to Flutter) cannot identify it as backend work, and the currently active Flutter gate would dispatch it to `two-model-coder` — whose session has no npm/node/tsc permission and whose Flutter-only red-form-check rejects Node-format evidence. Before scaffolding and dispatch, Script CEO must append a `manual: node` gate ledger entry (test_cmd `npm --prefix functions test --silent`, analyze_cmd `npm --prefix functions run build --silent`, detected=manual, lang=node) and dispatch under the `two-model-coder-node` operador, exactly as task 17 was dispatched. With lang=node, red-form-check has no Node classifier and coder-gate falls back to its non-empty evidence presence check, so Node RED/GREEN artifacts are accepted. A task-27 dispatch under the Flutter gate (`two-model-coder`, flutter test/analyze) is an orchestration/gate-routing defect to be corrected by installing the Node gate and re-dispatching; it must not be recorded as a task TEST_DEFECT or a terminal environment blocker, and no acceptance is relaxed to match the wrong gate.

tasks.title: Fix the task 13 backend entry-point composition
tasks.summary: Remediate the task 13 finding: functions/src/index.ts fails pm run build\ (tsc) because student, class, enrollment and attendance callables are wired with only datastore+clock while their handler interfaces require domain readers (directory/sessions/enrollments). Wire the readers those handler interfaces require, backed by the same Firestore datastore (small Firestore-backed adapters next to FirestoreDatastore, like FirestoreOverviewReader), so the Node gate compiles and every S11 callable stays exported exactly once with no unguarded provisioning endpoint.
acceptance: `npm --prefix functions run build` (tsc) exits 0 with no type errors in src/index.ts.

Every handler dependency interface is fully satisfied: studentDependencies supplies a StudentQueryReader (directory), class and enrollment dependencies supply a ClassSessionReader (sessions), attendanceDependencies supplies a ClassEnrollmentReader (enrollments) - all Firestore-backed like FirestoreDatastore/FirestoreOverviewReader, never in-memory seeds.
The exported callable set is unchanged: every S11 operation exported exactly once and no unguarded provisioning endpoint (the flutter suite test/app/backend_exports_test.dart stays green).
`npm --prefix functions test` passes across the full backend unit suite.
Node RED is evidenced before the fix (npm run build fails) and Node GREEN after (build + unit suite pass).
